meru-korea-isa-productive-finance-domest:
In the tax revision unveiled on August 3, the Korean government created a new account called the productive finance ISA.
Tax on interest and dividends inside it disappears and the lifetime ceiling doubles from the existing ISA, but the only things it may hold are domestic assets.

@@REF@@South Korea plans tax breaks to revive economic growth (UPI, 2026-08-03)|https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2026/08/03/special-taxation-act-tax-reform/2161785809142/|https://cdnph.upi.com/sv/ph/og/i/2161785809142/2026/1/17858092557035/v1.5/South-Korea-plans-tax-breaks-to-revive-economic-growth.jpg

An ISA is a tax favoured account that holds deposits, stocks and funds together and trims the tax on what they earn.
The existing Korean ISA exempts only the first 2 million won of gains and takes 9.9 percent of the rest separately, while the new account leaves interest and dividends untaxed with no ceiling at all.

Young savers get one more thing.
Anyone aged 15 to 34 with total salary of 75 million won or less can deduct 10 percent of the year's contributions from income. Paying in comes back as a deduction at year end settlement.

The annual contribution limit is 20 million won, and the account runs in three year contracts up to ten years in total.

## Looking only at the size of the bowl

@@BAR@@Existing ISA lifetime cap|100m won|10000|Productive finance ISA cap|200m won|20000|Japan's new NISA lifetime cap|18m yen (about 163m won)|16300@@On size alone the new Korean account is the bigger one. What the picture does not say is what may go inside it.@@Ministry of Economy and Finance 2026 tax revision (2026-08-03), Japan FSA NISA framework, converted at 906 won per 100 yen (checked 2026-08-05)

## What it is allowed to hold

The new account is limited to domestic assets: Korean stocks, domestic equity funds, and vehicles such as the National Growth Fund.
Exchange traded funds that track US indexes drop out even when they are listed in Seoul.

The target of that clause is not hard to see.
Korean retail investors held $161.1 billion of overseas stocks as of the end of September 2025, and the retail share of the country's outbound equity investment, less than one in ten before 2020, is now more than one in three.
The idea is to turn the flow that had been filling tax favoured accounts with US index funds back toward the domestic market.

@@REF@@Korea offers tax breaks to curb overseas stock outflows (Korea Herald, 2025-12-24)|https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10642876|https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/news/cms/2025/12/24/news-p.v1.20251224.c7ece11b937447eaafcfdba0cd307f0b_T1.jpg

Holding domestic assets only also means that when one country's market shakes, there is nothing inside the account to share the shock.
The saver takes the tax break and gives up the spread.

## What the 9.73 million existing accounts lose

The same revision reaches back into accounts that are already open.
At the end of June there were 9.73 million existing ISAs holding 73 trillion won.

First, unused contribution room can no longer be carried into the next year.
A saver who put in 5 million won this year could until now add the missing 15 million on top of the following year's room. The habit of catching up in a year when the bonus lands is closed off.

Second, a contract that could effectively be rolled forward indefinitely is now capped at five years.
The force of a tax favoured account comes from untaxed principal going straight back to work, and closing the account every five years shortens that runway.

@@CMP@@The government's account|Tax on interest and dividends is gone and the lifetime ceiling has doubled. With an income deduction for the young on top, the account got bigger.|Meru's reading|The assets it may hold are fenced into the domestic market, and existing accounts lost carryover and duration. The bowl grew while what goes in it shrank.

What splits the two readings of the same bill is whether you look at the size of the account or at the range of assets it is allowed to hold.

## Where the productive finance ISA meets the December Assembly

What exists today is a government proposal, and tax bills are normally settled in the regular National Assembly session in December.
Before deciding how to use the account, the thing to watch is not the size of the benefit but whether the domestic assets only clause survives intact.

If it passes as written, the practical answer is to run a tax favoured account for domestic assets next to an ordinary account for overseas indexes; if the Assembly opens the door to foreign assets, one account does the job.
Anyone already holding an ISA also has reason to weigh that this year is the last one with carryover in it.

The US services activity index stayed in expansion in July, but the employment component inside it dropped back into contraction.

In the same report business activity rose from 55.4 to 59.1 and new orders from 55.1 to 57.2. So this is not a case of activity drying up.

@@REF@@US service sector maintains strong growth pace in July (Reuters, 2026-08-05)|https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/us-service-sector-maintains-strong-growth-pace-in-july-4838224|https://i-invdn-com.investing.com/news/LYNXMPEBBR0PM_L.jpg

@@CHK@@Services PMI (July)|54.1|Consensus|54.5|Employment (July)|47.4|Employment (June)|51.2|Prices Paid (July)|70.3|Prices Paid (June)|67.7@@On the headline alone the index sits almost exactly where it did in June. What split was underneath, where employment and prices moved in opposite directions. The two things El-Erian singled out show up in the numbers.@@2026-08-05, ISM Services report as distributed on PR Newswire

## Why 50 is the line

This index does not measure amounts, it asks about direction.
Purchasing managers are asked whether things got better or worse than last month, and the share answering better becomes the index.

So 50 means as many firms said better as said worse, and below 50 means more firms said they cut than said they added.
An employment reading under 50 says more service firms shrank headcount than grew it. It does not say how many service jobs disappeared.

## Below 50 through the spring

@@TIME@@2026-03|Services employment at 45.2, first contraction of the year|2026-04|48.0, a second month of contraction|2026-05|47.9, a third month|2026-06|Back above 50 after one month|>2026-08-07|July jobs report@@Services employment sat below 50 through the spring, which makes June's bounce look closer to the exception.@@ISM Services monthly releases, March to August 2026

## The other jobs numbers that landed the same day

ADP, the payroll processor, counted 44,000 private jobs added in July. That is well short of the 65,000 the market was looking for, and June was revised down from 98,000 to 95,000.

@@REF@@ADP: Private sector hiring fell short of expectations last month (Yahoo Finance, 2026-08-05)|https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/adp-private-sector-hiring-fell-short-of-expectations-last-month-122648905.html|https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/663D1F11AB5F9508B7FE2370E2CB48EEDE961C72566EB9FAF2CEC6D4134263F1/subgraphmysterio/resizefill_w1200_h800;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fd29szjachogqwa.cloudfront.net%2Fimages%2F2026-08%2F1efbc6c5-ca6d-410e-886c-fac7471096c6

Job openings for June, published a day earlier, came in at 7.4 million, down from 7.5 million in May.
The side posting jobs and the side filling them are cooling together.

Meanwhile ADP had pay for people who changed jobs up 7.0 percent on a year earlier, the fastest since August last year, against 4.4 percent for those who stayed put.

## Prices went the other way

The services prices paid component reached 71.3 in May, the highest since August 2022. July sits just under that, the second highest of the past year.

The component has now pointed to rising prices for 110 months in a row. That is more than nine years without a month of falling service prices.

## The question the August 7 jobs report has to take

What the market is measuring now is not whether services are expanding but whether slower hiring has spread beyond services.
Consensus for Friday's report is 80,000 nonfarm jobs added and an unemployment rate holding at 4.2 percent.

Come in near that and the services employment dip stays a wobble in survey responses; come in well under and the combination of rising prices with cooling employment is confirmed.
The second one is the combination the Federal Reserve finds hardest to handle, because prices argue against cutting rates while employment argues for it.
pichai-gdm-reshuffle-dean-discovery-loop:
Google rewired the top of its AI organization in one announcement and waved off the chief scientist who had been there for 27 years.
Alphabet shares were reported trading around 4 percent lower on the day, in the $360s.

@@REF@@Alphabet Stock (GOOGL) Drops After Longtime Google AI Leaders Depart (TipRanks, 2026-08-05)|https://www.tipranks.com/news/alphabet-stock-googl-drops-after-longtime-google-ai-leaders-depart|https://blog.tipranks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/shutterstock_2712594637-750x406.jpg

## Who moved, who left

Demis Hassabis steps down as CEO of Google DeepMind and becomes Chair of the lab and Chief Scientist of Alphabet.
He keeps running Isomorphic Labs, the drug design company.

The seat where models actually get built goes to Koray Kavukcuoglu.
As SVP of Google DeepMind he takes Gemini model development, frontier research, and the Gemini app and developer teams, reporting straight to Pichai.
He has been at DeepMind for 13 years, and WaveNet, the speech synthesis system, and the DQN reinforcement learning model came out of his work.

@@REF@@Demis Hassabis drops DeepMind CEO role to become Chair and focus on AGI (9to5Google, 2026-08-05)|https://9to5google.com/2026/08/05/demis-hassabis-deepmind/|https://i0.wp.com/9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2025/04/Google-DeepMind-CEO-Demis-Hassabis-cover.jpg

Jeff Dean is leaving Google after 27 years.
He is starting a company with Sanjay Ghemawat, who joined in 1999 alongside him and has worked with him for more than 25 years.
Between them they built MapReduce, the Google File System, Bigtable, Spanner and TensorFlow.
The floor Google now stands on to process data and train models came out of their hands.
Oriol Vinyals, a Gemini co-lead, and Quoc Le, a co-founder of Google Brain, are reported to be joining them.

## Google is funding the company it is losing them to

The new firm is said to be a public benefit corporation.
That is a Delaware company form that must pursue a public purpose written into its charter alongside shareholder returns, and must report publicly on how that purpose is going.

Put simply, it is a for profit company that nails down in its charter what the profit is for.
Anthropic and Patagonia use the same structure.

Google is going in as a founding investor and supplying cloud capacity for the first year.
Radical Ventures and Khosla Ventures are reported to have invested alongside it, and the terms were not disclosed.
Reports name the company Discovery Loop. Pichai's own post does not name it.

## Not one day, but a year of this

@@TIME@@2025-06|Kavukcuoglu named Chief AI Architect at Alphabet|2026-06-23|Reports of DeepMind researchers moving to rivals|2026-07-30|Reports that the team behind AlphaFold was disbanded|2026-08-05|Reorganization announced, shares fall|>2026-10|Alphabet third quarter results@@This week reads less like a sudden break than the closing scene of departures that have been stacking up for over a year.@@Axios (2026-06-23), Technology.org (2026-07-30), Google blog (2026-08-05)

## The number Alphabet shows in October

In the same announcement Pichai said the Gemini app had passed 950 million monthly users and Gemma model downloads had passed 900 million.
The people changed; the spending did not. At July's second quarter results Alphabet raised its capital spending plan for the year to between $195 billion and $205 billion.

What an owner of this stock has reason to ask about is not the nameplate on the door but the pace at which models ship.
If development does not slip as researchers leave, this reads as a generational handover; if the capital spending plan steps back at the October results, it reads differently.
Google taking an investor's seat in its own people's new company gets re read at that point too. Either it bought with equity what it could not keep on payroll, or it decided that people may leave while the connection does not.

## Gold rose on the day peace news arrived
During Asian hours on August 5 gold pushed past $4,130 for a third straight session, and by New York hours The Kobeissi Letter reported it above $4,200, the highest since June 22.
The news moving through the market that day was that the US and Iran, with Oman mediating, were closing in on an interim deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

A safe-haven asset rose on a day when war risk was receding.
That happened because the channel the price travelled was not fear.

@@FLOW@@Hormuz deal nears|the US and Iran are reported close to an interim deal brokered by Oman|Oil falls|crude dropped about 5% the same day|Inflation expectations ease|cheaper energy pulls the expected path of prices down with it|Rate-hike odds shrink|the market prices less chance the Fed raises again@@What lifted gold was not risk. It was the arithmetic on the rate side.

Gold pays no interest.
Holding it means giving up the interest that same money would earn in bonds.
When rates look likely to rise further, the interest given up grows and holding gold gets harder. When rates look likely to stay put, that burden lightens.

What moved that day was not gold itself. It was the size of the interest being given up.

@@REF@@Asia-Pacific market news, gold jumped above $4,130 (investingLive, 2026-08-05)|https://investinglive.com/news/investinglive-asia-pacific-market-news-5-august-2026-gold-jumped-above-us-4130/|https://investinglive.com/cms/media/Processed/Categories/featured/Rapid%20gain%20for%20gold%20wrap%20chart%2005%20August%202026-featured-1785901317.jpg

That wrap also reports oil down roughly 5% on the day and the yen strengthening.
One piece of Hormuz news moved commodities and currencies at the same time.

## The condition written into the same UBS note
The path to that target is not a single leap. UBS wrote it as stages.

@@TIME@@>2026-09|$4,400|>2026-12|$4,600|>2027-03|$5,000|>2027-06|$5,200@@Each waypoint has to hold for the next one to stand. Miss the September number and everything behind it slides.@@Retrieved 2026-08-05 · UBS forecast path as reported by investingLive on 2026-08-03

And there is a condition attached in front of it.
UBS said gold could be pushed down toward $3,850 if markets keep pricing possible rate increases this year and investment appetite stays soft.

That condition runs straight into today's story.
If the Hormuz deal actually lands and inflation expectations come down, the very condition UBS worried about weakens. If the deal slips and oil retraces, the condition comes back to life.
The same event is shaking the target and the downside case at once.

## The half Hanke did not pass along
Hanke's post carries the target and not the downside case.
Target and downside case are consecutive sentences in one note, and lifting only one of them turns a forecast into a recommendation.

Where this card gets marked is clear enough.
If gold reaches the target UBS wrote down by June 2027, that path was right. If it prints the downside level first, the other sentence in the same note was right.
Either way, one fact stays: today's level is below the high set in January. Not reading a recovery as a rally is the first condition for reading this forecast at all.
jukan-solidigm-pre-ipo-50-trillion-tag:
Solidigm, SK hynix's US subsidiary, is raising money ahead of a Nasdaq listing.
The round is being marketed at a valuation of roughly 50 trillion won, and it is seeking up to 10 trillion won.

@@REF@@SK hynix-owned Solidigm seeks up to $7bn in pre-IPO share sale (KED Global, 2026-08-05)|https://www.kedglobal.com/pre-ipos/newsView/ked202608050008|https://www.kedglobal.com/data/ked/image/2026/08/05/ked202608050037.png

The company exists because SK hynix bought Intel's NAND business outright.
The price it paid was $8.85 billion.

@@BAR@@Total paid for Intel's NAND business|$8.85bn|88.5|Pre-IPO target valuation|about $35bn|350@@Between the price paid and the price now being asked sits one full cycle in NAND.@@Retrieved 2026-08-05 · deal value from Tom's Hardware 2025-03-28, target valuation from KED Global's dollar conversion

## What NAND actually does
NAND is the chip that keeps the photos on your phone and the files on your laptop from disappearing.
It is storage memory that holds its contents with the power off, and in a data centre it is packed into a box and plugged into a server.
That box is an SSD, and the enterprise version has its own name, eSSD.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/USB_flash_drive.JPG/500px-USB_flash_drive.JPG|What sits inside a USB stick is NAND. A data centre packs the same chip into a much larger box and plugs it into a server.|Nrbelex · CC BY-SA 3.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:USB_flash_drive.JPG

That box is what Solidigm sells.

## What changed since Intel sold
Intel put this business up for sale when NAND was not making money.
Prices swung hard while the cost of building capacity kept climbing, so Intel chose to leave the business entirely.

The picture is now inverted.
AI servers need somewhere to keep the data their models read, and enterprise SSD contract prices rose roughly 80% in the first quarter of 2026 alone.
In that same quarter the top five vendors booked a record $18.46 billion in enterprise SSD revenue.

@@SHARE@@Samsung|$7.05bn|7.05|SK hynix Group|$4.64bn|4.64|Micron|$3.09bn|3.09|Kioxia and SanDisk|$3.69bn|3.69@@The top two take two thirds of this market, and SK hynix Group's share already contains Solidigm.@@Retrieved 2026-08-05 · TrendForce release of 2026-06-11, based on 1Q26 revenue

## The QLC fork
NAND types are separated by how many bits go into one storage cell.
TLC holds three bits, QLC holds four. The more bits per cell, the more capacity in the same area, and the less rewriting the cell survives.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/Cell_types_SLC-PLC_in_comparison_20211102.svg/1280px-Cell_types_SLC-PLC_in_comparison_20211102.svg.png|How many bits go into one cell decides the character of the NAND. QLC, the type Solidigm is pushing, sits at the far right.|PantheraLeo1359531 · CC0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cell_types_SLC-PLC_in_comparison_20211102.svg

What AI servers mostly do is read stored data over and over.
When the erase and rewrite count is low, QLC's weakness barely shows and only its advantage remains, which is more capacity for the same money.
TrendForce described SK hynix Group's first quarter as a division of labour, with Solidigm ramping QLC shipments while SK hynix itself expanded TLC.

@@REF@@Intel and SK hynix close NAND business deal (Tom's Hardware, 2025-03-28)|https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/ssds/intel-and-sk-hynix-close-nand-business-deal-intel-gets-usd1-9-billion-sk-hynix-gets-ip-and-employees|https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/oeBcD8HLoUmAPSKy5xtMfd.png

That article carries one more point worth lifting.
The deal did not finish in 2021. It was split into two closings, and the NAND patents and the research staff only crossed over on March 27, 2025.
Until then Solidigm had the fab and the products but did not own the underlying technology.

## What Solidigm is being priced at
Seen from the pricing side, NAND is at the top of its range right now.
Whether the listed market accepts a number set at the peak of a boom is a separate question.

This is the fork.
If the pre-IPO round closes near its target and a Nasdaq listing follows, SK hynix will have turned one business bought from Intel into several times its purchase price in cash and equity value.
If the raise or the valuation falls short, or the round slips, the message is that the market reads today's NAND prices as the top of a cycle.
For an investor the question that splits here is whether SK hynix shares are already pricing a memory boom or the re-rating of a single subsidiary.
kobeissi-anthropic-custom-silicon-multi-:
Anthropic has confirmed that it will design the chips that run Claude itself.
Yet the same announcement stated that hardware from Amazon's AWS, Google, Nvidia and AMD will remain essential.

@@REF@@Anthropic is hiring an AI chip design team (TechCrunch, 2026-08-05)|https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/05/anthropic-is-hiring-an-ai-chip-design-team/|https://techcrunch.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/GettyImages-1484622878.jpeg?resize=1200,800

A company that says it will build its own chips also says it will keep buying everyone else's.
The two statements do not collide. What sits between them is the time it takes for a chip that is only now being designed to end up in a live server.

## Why build silicon now
The cost of running a model like Claude splits into two parts.
There is the cost of training the model, and there is the cost incurred every time the finished model answers a user.
The second one is called inference, and it keeps growing as long as users keep arriving.

Training ends once. Inference is money that goes out every day the service is alive.
So shaving even a few percent off the electricity and time behind a single answer changes the shape of the whole income statement.

A general-purpose accelerator is built to handle both training and inference reasonably well.
A chip cut to fit one company's own model can drop the functions that model never uses, and save power and silicon area in the process.
That is what Anthropic means when it says it will co-design hardware and models.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/NVIDIA_GPU.jpg/960px-NVIDIA_GPU.jpg|What runs Claude today is an accelerator board somebody else designed and sold. What Anthropic wants to draw is its own chip for that slot.|Mickael Courtiade · CC BY 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NVIDIA_GPU.jpg

## Years just to reach tape-out
A chip does not appear the moment the design is finished.
Handing the circuit layout to a fab and printing the first prototype is called tape-out.
Reaching that step usually takes a new team years, and validation and production ramp come after it.

A chip from a team that is only now posting job ads is that far away from carrying a service.

Until then the chips that run Claude still have to be bought.
That is why Anthropic talks about using hardware from several vendors at once. The in-house chip is not a replacement for what it runs today. It is something that will sit beside it years from now.

## What the job ad asks for
The listed salary runs from $320,000 to $485,000.
The requirement is not publications but direct personal experience taking a chip through tape-out and out the door.
Anthropic is looking for people who have shipped, not people who have studied.

@@REF@@Anthropic publicly reveals custom chip plans for the first time, offering up to $485,000 a year (BigGo Finance, 2026-08-05)|https://finance.biggo.com/news/13056eb1-c5d9-46eb-93f9-d522773cd4ec|https://img.biggo.com/blW0HJjL62s_IAo9-QGRKmk8XDBO6qi-K-o3jjMJhxk/fit/1200/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA4LzEzMDU2ZWIxLWM1ZDktNDZlYi05M2Y5LWQ1MjI3NzNjZDRlY18xNzg1OTM3MzI3X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.jpg

The ad also tells you there is no semiconductor organisation inside the company yet.
Design tools, fab agreements and verification staff all still have to be brought in from outside.

@@TIME@@2024-11|Amazon invests a further $4bn in Anthropic and AWS becomes its primary cloud|2025-10|Anthropic agrees to take up to one million of Google's TPUs|2026-06|OpenAI unveils Jalapeno, an inference chip built with Broadcom|2026-08-05|Anthropic confirms it is hiring an in-house chip design team@@A company that got this far on borrowed silicon has moved one seat toward the drawing board.@@Retrieved 2026-08-05 · compiled from TechCrunch, Reuters and Malay Mail reports

## What Anthropic is buying with a chip
The point of custom silicon is unit cost, not a place on a performance table.
OpenAI said in June that Jalapeno cut its costs in half. That figure is OpenAI's own claim and no outside verification has appeared.

The Kobeissi Letter called in-house AI chips the next big trend.
If that holds, then from the seller's side of the accelerator market, the largest customers are each assembling a design team.

The line to watch from here is the price list.
If Anthropic says its own chip is in production service and Claude's pricing or throughput moves with it, this hiring round changed the cost structure. If the rates and limits stay where they are long after the chip talk, this stage is closer to leverage in a supplier negotiation.
When the renter starts building, whether price or volume moves first is what shows up here.
jukan-samsung-5nm-pitch-sf5a-auto-line-s:
The node Samsung Foundry is now putting in front of customers is neither 2nm nor 4nm. It is 5nm.
With the 4nm line booked out through next year, the sales pitch has shifted to offering fabless customers who cannot absorb the cost of a finer node the generation below it, where yields are already settled.

@@BAR@@TSMC|70.4%|70.4|Samsung Foundry|7.1%|7.1@@Filling a line and winning a customer are different things. This is still the distance between the two companies.@@Retrieved 2026-08-05 · TrendForce release of 2026-03-12, based on 4Q25 revenue

@@REF@@AI demand drives 4Q25 global top 10 foundry revenue up 2.6% QoQ, Samsung gains share (TrendForce, 2026-03-12)|https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260312-12965.html|https://img.trendforce.com/EDM/2026/03/20260312_163034_3.jpg

## Who filled the 4nm line
The largest customer filling that line is not an outside fabless firm. It is the memory division of the same company.
HBM is a stack of DRAM layers, and the board at the very bottom that organises the signals and sends them out is the base die.
Samsung builds that board not on a memory process but on the foundry's 4nm logic process.

So the better memory sells, the fuller the foundry line gets.

On top of that, industry sources say, came volume from Nvidia's dedicated inference chip.
Nvidia licensed Groq's technology in December 2025 and unveiled the Groq 3 LPU at GTC in March 2026, a chip that uses no HBM at all and instead keeps 500 megabytes of SRAM on the die itself.
The board that holds up HBM and the chip that refuses to use HBM are coming off the same 4nm line.

@@REF@@GTC 2026 keynote: long live the inference king (EE Times, 2026-03-20)|https://www.eetimes.com/gtc-2026-keynote-long-live-the-inference-king/|https://www.eetimes.com/wp-content/uploads/Inference-King-sq.jpg

That article describes the Groq 3 LPU as a chip paired with Rubin GPUs and handed only the token-generation work.
It fills in the part the original post names and moves past.

## The road the pushed-out customers take

@@FLOW@@TSMC 3-5nm full|reported effectively booked through 2026|Large customers first|Apple, Qualcomm and Nvidia take the wafers ahead of others|Smaller customers pushed out|Chinese and Indian fabless firms look for another line|Samsung 5nm|takes that volume on a process whose yields are settled@@What Samsung is gaining right now is not leading-edge orders but the seats everyone else left behind.

The claim that Chinese and Indian fabless firms are coming to Samsung's 5nm to work around sanctions comes from a Samsung supply-chain partner, quoted anonymously.
English-language reporting confirms only part of it.
China's NIO already uses Samsung 5nm for its autonomous driving chip, and Samsung is reported to be in talks with BYD on autonomous driving SoCs.
No Indian customer is named anywhere.

## SF5A stands between cars and servers
The 5nm line is classified as SF5A, a process dedicated to automotive.

## Why a rising yen pushes US stocks down

Borrowing yen cheaply in Japan, converting it into dollars and parking it in US Treasuries or equities is called a carry trade.
Pay 1 percent to borrow and earn 4 percent where the money sits, and 3 percentage points a year accrue while you do nothing.
If the yen is weaker when the loan comes due, the exchange rate hands over a second profit.

The catch is that this trade is usually run on five to ten times the trader's own money.

When the yen rises quickly, the sequence runs like this.
The carry position takes a mark to market loss first, and when the collateral falls short a demand for more margin arrives.
If fresh money is hard to find, the US stocks and bonds in the account get sold.
The proceeds have to be turned back into yen to repay the loan, so the bid for yen grows again.
The yen ticks up once more, another trader's stop is touched, and the same loop starts over from the top.

That is why an unwind does not arrive slowly over months but lands in a few days.

## Why yields and stocks now move apart

A correlation is a single number between -1 and 1 that measures how closely two things move together.
At 1 they always move in the same direction, at -1 always in opposite directions, and at 0 they have nothing to do with each other.

For more than a decade before 2020 this number was positive.
Rising yields signalled a stronger economy, and a stronger economy meant companies earned more, so share prices rose alongside them.

That link has broken.

Today, when yields rise stocks give way, and when yields fall stocks hold up.
August 4 in New York looked exactly like that: the S&P 500 closed at a record 7,736.52 while the 10-year yield slipped to 4.6%.

The Kobeissi Letter names inflation uncertainty and fiscal concerns side by side as the cause.

The nominal 10-year yield was 4.7% as of August 3.

The first is called breakeven inflation, the second the real yield.
Breakeven inflation sat at 2.2% on August 4, close enough to the Fed's 2% target, while the real yield was 2.4%.

One is to stop issuing sanctions as a single large package and instead handle them in small thematic batches, each agreed on its own.
The other is to move some foreign-policy decisions from unanimity to qualified majority voting.
Both read on the surface as procedural tuning meant to speed approval up.
The working effect lies elsewhere, in narrowing the moments at which a member state can reach for its veto.

One point has to be made here for the rest to follow.
The veto is a power the treaties handed to member states, so removing it means amending the treaties, and amending the treaties requires unanimity again.

A data center on the ground moves heat into air or water and dumps it outside.

Add the solar arrays that make the electricity and the thing ends up 70 meters across and 20 meters tall.
Put simply, it is running a server in a room with no air to blow, so the panel that throws heat away has to be as large as the machine itself.

## How a 3-percent asset pays double digits

@@FLOW@@Deposit the Treasury token|It keeps earning while being pledged|Borrow stablecoins|A fraction of the pledged value|Buy more Treasury tokens|The same asset is stacked one layer deeper|Deposit again|The principal earning interest is larger when the loop restarts@@The route matters because the yield is not coming out of the asset. The original post says that repeating this automatically on venues such as Jupiter can push annualised yields above 10%.

What short-dated US Treasuries actually pay is nowhere near that.
The three-month Treasury bill rate published by the St. Louis Fed stood at 3.6% in the middle of May.
Buying the same asset again with borrowed money and pledging it once more, a repetition usually called looping, fills the gap.
Each turn enlarges the principal that earns interest, and the same Treasury gets counted as collateral twice or three times.
Margin lending in equities and the bond repo market already work this way; what is new is that code, not a person, runs the loop.

What sets the character of this market is that when collateral loses value, the seller is code rather than a person.

The line to watch is the rate paid to borrow stablecoins.
While that rate sits below the Treasury coupon the loop turns, and the moment it rises above the coupon every turn adds a loss.

The contract to sell the capacity is already signed, while the date on which the capacity comes into existence is still ahead.

Markets picked the most certain link in the chain first.

Volta, the company that won the contract, is private and carries no price at all.

In the middle of that route stands a company with no operating record, and if it stumbles the power and the buildings stay with Bitdeer while the contract goes back to the negotiating table.

## What does sold out actually mean
It does not mean there is nothing to buy. It means the order of who gets served first is already fixed.

Memory makers are shipping only 60% to 70% of the volumes buyers asked for.
A company that requested 100 receives 65.
Cloud providers and AI firms are filled first, smartphone and PC makers come next.
Module houses stand behind them, and the 30% figure from Apacer is the view from the end of that line.

One more thing follows from this.
A company that has not locked its volumes knows that stepping in now would shrink the allocations of firms already served.
So everyone moves quietly. Saying out loud that you are short brings the competition running.

## The price is set when the goods ship
The part that stays out of view here is price.

Volumes are largely settled, but the actual price is said to be fixed only closer to delivery.
The buyer has locked the quantity and not the cost.
A normal contract ties the two together. Right now the seller has the power to leave price for later.
For a device maker that has to model 2027 costs today, holding an allocation is not by itself a reason to relax.

## NAND is not the same picture as DRAM
The original post puts DRAM and NAND on one line and calls both sold out. That is where readings part.

@@REF@@DRAM buyers face two more years of scarcity as NAND tilts toward surplus, TrendForce outlook (TechTimes, 2026-07-31)|https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322399/20260731/dram-buyers-face-two-more-years-scarcity-nand-tilts-toward-surplus.htm|https://d.techtimes.com/en/full/470721/micron-232-layer-nand-manufacturing.png

In its July 30 outlook TrendForce saw the DRAM balance deteriorating further through 2027.
NAND, by contrast, could swing to a surplus in 2027.
Taller stacks are the reason: SK hynix V8 at 321 layers, Samsung V9 above 290, Kioxia BiCS10 at 332 layers all pull more capacity out of the same fab.

@@CMP@@Serenity's reading|You cannot call something a glut when it is already sold out. The shortage is deepening, not easing.|TrendForce's reading|True for DRAM. NAND gains capacity from taller stacks and may run long in the second half of 2027.
The same sold out fact splits depending on whether you look only at DRAM or count NAND as well.

## The split comes in NAND in late 2027
On DRAM the two readings do not fight. The fight is over NAND.

TrendForce attached a condition of its own. If AI agents spread quickly and start parking their conversation histories on storage, the added NAND capacity may simply be absorbed.
In that case the swing to surplus never arrives.

If NAND turns long in the second half of 2027, this sold out moment was a DRAM story all along. If it stays short, memory moved as one.
Either way the buyer is left holding volume without holding price.
